newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline ends lower on Trainer restart.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline ends lower on Trainer restart.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline ended lower Thursday after Tosco Corp said it reopened its Trainer, Pennsylvania refinery which will add about 100,000 barrels a day of gasoline to the market.
June gasoline ended 0.34 cent a gallon lower at 64.04 cents. June crude finished nine cents a barrel lower at $21.30 while June heating oil ended 0.06 cent a gallon up at 56.48 cents.
Dealers said gasoline's losses were limited by the market's anticipation of the refinery's restart for several months.

"Gasoline came off after the Trainer news, but it was mostly discounted already," said Mark Turner, vice president of inventory product management at Transmontaigne Products Services Inc in Fayettville, Arkansas.
The Trainer refinery had been shut since early 1996 for a $50 million modernization after Tosco acquired the plant from British Petroleum.
Tosco had said the official restart would be mid-May and dealers had known the refinery, which has total capacity of 150,000 barrels per day, was being tested by Tosco this week.
Gasoline's losses were also limited by news Phillips Petroleum Co's 205,000 barrel per day Sweeny, Texas refinery was shut for three to seven days.
Philips said the refinery was shut due to a power outage in the refinery's local area.
Meanwhile, dealers said spot crude was pressured by a commercial player selling the June/July spread which saw its backwardation narrow to one cent from 10 cents Wednesday.
Backwardation indicates the nearer contract in time is more expensive than the later one.
